Query a remote DuckDB server as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__duckdb.R
oauth_db_duckdb.Rd

Attach a DuckDB Quack server using the visitor's OAuth access token and query its tables with DBI or dbplyr. The server must validate OAuth tokens, for example with the quack_oauth extension.

Usage

oauth_db_duckdb(
  authorization,
  host,
  port = 9494L,
  schema = "main",
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  allow_local_http = FALSE,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

host

One TCP hostname or address. Enclose IPv6 addresses in brackets.

port

Quack server or TLS proxy port, default 9494.

schema

Default schema in the remote database, default "main".

ca_bundle

Optional CA certificate bundle path for a private server CA.

allow_local_http

Allow unencrypted HTTP for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. Defaults to FALSE; use only for local development.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning a DuckDB DBI connection.

Details

Install duckdb 1.5.3 or later and its matching quack and httpfs extensions. Provision them before starting the app with INSTALL quack and INSTALL httpfs in DuckDB. The helper loads them in a separate in-memory database for each connection. TLS and certificate verification are required, including on loopback unless allow_local_http = TRUE. Use a certificate trusted by the DuckDB client.

shinyOAuth manages sign-in and token renewal. Only the access token is passed to Quack; the client does not need quack_oauth or persistent secrets. Configure the server's trusted issuer, audience and authorization policy.

Call con() before each operation. A changed access token replaces the connection because Quack authenticates at attachment time. This also ends any transaction on the old connection. Account changes, lost permissions, sign-out and session end shut down the private DuckDB instance. Queries and failed statements are never replayed by the helper.

The remote catalog is attached as oauth_remote and selected as the default database, so unqualified table names use its selected schema. SQL runs through DuckDB's attached-catalog interface; local expressions and functions can still execute on the client.

See also

vignette("duckdb", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has server requirements, sign-in setup and a complete app. oauth_db_demo() runs a local Quack and Keycloak example.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside server(), using a client for the Quack server's issuer and audience:
con <- oauth_db_duckdb(
  auth$connection, host = "duckdb.example.org", port = 443,
  required_scopes = "quack:read"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM orders LIMIT 20")
})
} # }
